observations: Close-up of a used car engine bay/assembly, partially disassembled or pulled for sale
Visible alternator with serpentine belt, wiring harness with multiple connectors, exhaust manifold or downpipe, coolant/oil residue consistent with a used part
General grime and wear typical of a 'tokunbo' (used import) engine
No engine code, VIN, part number, or manufacturer plate legible anywhere in the frame
Watermark reads 'CAMON 40' (a phone model watermark, not an item brand) plus camera EXIF data overlay

claims.evidence: No import documentation, auction sticker, or chassis tag visible in photo 0
No written warranty, receipt, or shop signage shown in photo 0

risks.risk: Exact engine make/model/displacement cannot be confirmed, which drives most of the price
risks.proof: Clear shot of the engine code sticker/stamp, or a wide shot showing the full block with any casting numbers
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all until engine identity is known

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal faults (compression, timing, bearings)
risks.proof: Video of the engine running/idling with sound

risks.risk: Alternator and wiring harness condition/functionality unknown
risks.proof: Photo of alternator bench-test or multimeter reading showing output voltage

risks.risk: Mileage and prior usage history unverifiable
risks.proof: Odometer photo from donor vehicle or import paperwork

risks.risk: Fitment to buyer's specific car model unconfirmed
risks.proof: Chassis number or model-year match from seller
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified fitment, buyer risk

proof_requests: Close-up of the engine code/casting number stamped on the block
Video of the engine running to confirm it starts and idles smoothly
Any import/auction sheet or documentation showing 'Japan direct' origin
Photo of alternator output test (multimeter) and full wiring harness
Confirmation of which car make/model/year this engine is pulled from
response.reason: The photo shows a used engine assembly but no engine code, car model, or running proof is visible, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without knowing what engine this actually is and whether it runs.
